frame.note: manifest differs from the V11 run (CA register 1.1.2); frame size identical

returnBasis: PRICE_RETURN on both sides; SPY_TR = SPY price + N-30D distributions (reference only)

seriesDefinitions.SPY_W: SPY price return at the weekly bar dates
seriesDefinitions.EW_ALL: equal-weighted all PIT S&P 500 members (holdings returns, scenario)
seriesDefinitions.EW_WITH_H: equal-weighted members WITH our series, holdings return
seriesDefinitions.EW_FRAME: equal-weighted survivor frame (all frame listings with a bar at t0, V10/V11 population), weekly-series return, period buy-and-hold
seriesDefinitions.EW_FRAME_WREB: V11 definition: weekly rebalanced equal-weighted frame index between the same bar dates

identity: EW_FRAME - SPY = (EW_FRAME - EW_WITH_S) [universe: survivor titles outside the index] + (EW_WITH_S - EW_WITH_H) [measurement: weekly series vs holdings, dates] + (EW_WITH_H - EW_ALL) [survivorship INSIDE the index] + (EW_ALL - SPY) [equal weighting inside the index]; plus SPY_TR - SPY [benchmark definition] and EW_FRAME_WREB - EW_FRAME [rebalancing frequency]. Exact per period.
correction: Korrektur nach unabhaengiger Pruefung: SPXPOP 1.1.1 (Broadcom-Identitaetsbruch u. a.), Szenarien FATE/UPPER, Spanne ab 2013-03 (SPXPOP-Regel 1.0.1), Szenario-Bezeichnungen (amendment-1.1.0.json)

scenarios.ZERO: point convention: bounded exits at 0 % (last holdings price), ambiguous CA at the midpoint - NOT a bound
scenarios.LOWER: all bounded exits at -100 %, ambiguous CA at the lower bound - gives the UPPER bound of the survivorship term (EW_WITH_H - EW_ALL) and the lower bound of EW_ALL/CW_ALL
scenarios.FATE: exits by documented fate: takeover -> typical premium of documented takeovers (takeoverPremium.median), delisting/bankruptcy -> -100 %, index change -> population period return, unknown fate -> 0 %; ambiguous CA midpoint - evidence-based point estimate
scenarios.UPPER: every bounded exit at max(takeover premium p75, population period return), ambiguous CA at the upper bound - gives the lower end of the survivorship term
